raw_case_text:
A 40-year-old male who was 178-cm tall and 100-kg in weight was admitted to a local hospital in November 2013 year with fever (39  C), diarrhea, an oxygen saturation of 60%, and the gradual onset of dyspnea, confusion, and shock. Physical examination revealed bleeding spots on the chest and abdomen and florid spots on the lower limbs. Laboratory tests revealed a platelet count (PLT) of 26 x 109/L, a blood urea nitrogen (BUN) level of 13.9 mmol/L, a creatinine (CRE) level of 330 mumol/L, a urine protein level of 3+, and positivity for the HFRS anti-IgM antibody. The patient had a history of hypertension (usual blood pressure 160/100 mmHg) and fatty liver. The patient was diagnosed with HFRS and treated with ventilator-assisted ventilation, fluid replacement, and norepinephrine to increase the blood pressure. He was admitted to the Department of Intensive Care at The First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University with HFRS, septic shock, decompensated metabolic acidosis, AKI, and multiple organ failure. The laboratory test results after admission into the ICU are listed in Table 1. Because of AKI and anuria, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) was administered, and ventilator-assisted ventilation, sedation and analgesia, fluid replacement, norepinephrine to increase the blood pressure, and plasma and platelet transfusions were administered.
On day 1 of admission, the left nasal cavity was filled with an expanded sponge because of coagulation disorders complicated by left nasal cavity bleeding. On the second day after the nasal filling, the left nasal alar became purple and swollen (Figure 1). Massive nasal necrotic lesions rapidly occurred the next day. Microbial cultures from the lesion samples revealed the growth of mucormycetes (Figure 2). The strain was identified as Rhizopus oryzae complex by mass spectrometry (Figure 3). Bronchofiberoptic bronchoalveolar lavage fluid culture confirmed Aspergillus growth, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) strains identified Aspergillus fumigatus. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid galactomannan (GM) 1.29 (GM < 1.0 negative), and serum GM 4.99 (GM < 0.5 negative). The patient was diagnosed with rhinomucormycosis and pulmonary aspergillosis, and systemic caspofungin and voriconazole were administered. The therapeutic dose was adjusted according to organ function and drug characteristics of the patients. Caspofungin: loading dose: 70 mg/d, qd; post-35 mg/d, ivgtt; voriconazole: loading dose: 400 mg/12 h, ivgtt, bid, post-100 mg/12 h, ivgtt. Because the patient had developed multiple organ failure, such as liver and kidney failure, intravenous amphotericin B treatment was not possible. To avoid further impairment of the liver function, we developed a local treatment regimen for nasal mucormycosis. The nasal cavity was rinsed with 10 mL saline, kept dry for 1 h, then filled with a sterile dressing containing 2.5 mg/mL amphotericin B for 4 h, and finally filled with a sterile dressing containing 5% sodium bicarbonate for 1 h. These procedures were administered every 6 h. After 12 days, the left nasal scab fell off, and a large tissue defect remained (Figure 4). Computed tomography revealed no orbitocerebral involvement during the treatment.    
After the treatment, the patient 's condition gradually stabilized, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid culture revealed no fungal growth, and lung imaging findings gradually returned to normal. Urine output and renal function recovered after weaning from the ventilator (day 11), discontinuation of caspofungin (day 13), and discontinuation of voriconazole (day 14). The patient recovered on day 28 and was discharged. During 2 years of follow-up, the patient exhibited no further signs of rhinomucormycosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old obese male with severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, septic shock, and anuric acute kidney injury developed rapid purple swelling and massive necrosis of his left nasal ala 2 days after anterior nasal sponge packing for epistaxis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Admitted in November 2013 with high fever (39 C), diarrhea, severe hypoxemia (SpO2 60%), confusion, shock, thrombocytopenia, and anuric acute kidney injury due to serologically confirmed hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), the patient was placed on mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, and CRRT in the ICU. On ICU day 1, an expandable nasal sponge was packed into the left nasal cavity for coagulopathic epistaxis; 2 days later, the left nasal ala became violaceous and edematous and rapidly progressed the next day to massive full-thickness nasal necrosis alongside pulmonary fungal infection.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertension (baseline BP 160/100 mmHg), obesity (height 178 cm, weight 100 kg), and fatty liver.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever (39 C), diarrhea, dyspnea, confusion, epistaxis, and rapid left nasal necrosis.

objective.physical_examination: Height 178 cm, weight 100 kg; initial exam showed fever (39 C), SpO2 60%, shock, petechial bleeding spots on the chest and abdomen, and florid ecchymotic spots on the lower extremities. On ICU day 2-3 after left nasal packing, the left nasal ala developed purple swelling that rapidly evolved into a black necrotic eschar, leaving a full-thickness left nasal alar tissue defect when the scab detached after 12 days of topical therapy.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial labs showed severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 26 x 10^9/L), BUN 13.9 mmol/L, serum creatinine 330 umol/L (with anuria), 3+ proteinuria, decompensated metabolic acidosis, hepatic and renal dysfunction, and positive serum anti-HFRS IgM antibody.
objective.advanced_workup: Cultures and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry of the necrotic left nasal lesion isolated Rhizopus oryzae complex (rhinomucormycosis), while head/sinus CT showed no orbitocerebral extension. Concurrently, fiberoptic bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) culture and PCR identified Aspergillus fumigatus, with positive BALF galactomannan (1.29; cutoff <1.0) and markedly elevated serum galactomannan (4.99; cutoff <0.5).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) complicated by dual invasive fungal superinfection: nasal packing-associated cutaneous/nasal Rhizopus oryzae complex mucormycosis and invasive pulmonary Aspergillus fumigatus infection (confirmed by nasal wound culture/mass spectrometry, BALF culture and PCR for A. fumigatus, BALF GM 1.29, and serum GM 4.99). Because hepatic and anuric renal failure precluded systemic intravenous amphotericin B, he was treated with organ-adjusted intravenous caspofungin (70 mg loading, then 35 mg/day for 13 days) and intravenous voriconazole (400 mg q12h loading, then 100 mg q12h for 14 days) combined with an every-6-hour topical nasal regimen (10 mL saline rinse, 1-hour drying, 4-hour packing with 2.5 mg/mL amphotericin B gauze, and 1-hour packing with 5% sodium bicarbonate gauze), achieving sloughing of the nasal eschar at day 12, negative repeat BALF cultures, ventilator weaning on day 11, full renal recovery, discharge on day 28, and 2 years of recurrence-free follow-up.
